title: Alchymey teuczsch, alchemical recipe book, East Bavaria 1426, Heidelberg Cod. Pal. germ. 597 (DECODE R2876)

steps.what: IIIF manifest and images of the 85 written leaves fetched with a browser User-Agent; catalogue pp. 256-261, Bischoff 1954 and Wattenbach's pages obtained.
Found Wattenbach 1869, Eis and the 2014 catalogue: the ciphers were broken in 1869. The candidate list's 'ff. 70-71' shown to be Bischoff's item numbers, not folios.
Survey of all 85 leaves (three agents) locating every cipher run: f. 1r, ff. 5v-6r, 6v, 7r-22r, 9r, 44v, 46r-v, 54r-61r, 79ar, 91v, 93r.
Key A: the compiler's struck 24-sign alphabet on f. 1r read after removing the strike line (seg2.py), aligned with Wattenbach's reading 'abcdefghiklmnopqrsstuwschch'.
Key A checked on f. 1r l. 2 'hab es' and the f. 11r heading 'niklas gank?icz' (modern pencil gloss 'Niklas Gankwiz'); one sign unread.
Key B: f. 6v aligned glyph by glyph (seg.py) against Wattenbach's printed invocation; 19 values; f. 91v found to be the same set in abc order.
Set C: 11 letters fixed from the catalogue's f. 93r reading 'in dem caichen' and Wattenbach's f. 1r l. 1 'Das ist ein abc'; s and t from one word each.

One-key review (Lasry's rule, 14 Oct 2026): the notebook uses three independent sign alphabets, so the outcome is given per part: key A and key B read from Wattenbach's 1869 decipherment (key A partial, the recipe cipher untranscribed; key B complete), set C key recovered from the 2014 catalogue's reading of f. 93r (external plaintext), partial. Credits scoped per alphabet.

outcome.method_basis: Wattenbach broke the ciphers in 1869 and printed plaintexts of ff. 1r, 5v, 6v, and the 2014 Heidelberg catalogue reads f. 93r; the project recovered the sign alphabets from the images by aligning them with those printed readings (external plaintext) and the compiler's own f. 1r alphabet.
outcome.notes: Read by Wattenbach 1869; added here: the alphabets recovered from the images and checked, set C partly fixed, the survey, the folio correction. Open: no continuous transcription of the recipe cipher (ff. 7r-22r, 46r-v, 54r-61r), f. 9r ll. 7-12, the f. 6r glossary or f. 44v; key A m-ch unchecked on running text. Three sign alphabets, results per part in outcome.parts (one-key review, 14 Oct 2026): set C's values come from the 2014 catalogue crib, not from Wattenbach.

credits.note: broke the ciphers in 1869; plaintexts of f. 1r (key A, and set C ll. 1-2) and f. 6v (key B) used to align the sign alphabets
credits.source: Wattenbach, Anzeiger für Kunde der deutschen Vorzeit NF 16 (1869), cols. 264-268

credits.note: 2014 Heidelberg catalogue reading of f. 93r, used as crib for set C only (Kalning, Miller, Zimmermann)
credits.source: Kalning, Miller, Zimmermann, Cod. Pal. germ. 496-670 (2014), pp. 257-260

parts.label: key A, the compiler's 24-sign 'new abc' (f. 1r)
parts.records: Cod. Pal. germ. 597: f. 1r ll. 3-4 (the alphabet), recipe names ff. 7r-22r, 46r-v, 54r-61r, f. 9r ll. 7-12, part of ff. 5v-6r
parts.basis: Wattenbach 1869 printed the f. 1r plaintext; the 24-sign alphabet recovered here from the image (a-l grade H, m-ch C), checked on 'hab es' and the f. 11r heading 'niklas gank?icz'; the recipe cipher has no continuous transcription, so the extent is partial

parts.label: key B, stroke and figure signs (ff. 6v, 91v)
parts.records: f. 6v invocation (three lines); f. 91v the same set in abc order
parts.basis: Wattenbach 1869 printed the f. 6v plaintext ('In dem namen des faters ...'); aligned sign by sign here, 19 values; f. 91v agrees on its first signs

parts.label: set C, boxes, stars and T (ff. 1r ll. 1-2, 5v-6r, 44v, 93r)
parts.records: f. 93r (two lines), f. 1r ll. 1-2; f. 44v and the f. 6r glossary unread
parts.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
parts.basis: values fixed from the 2014 Heidelberg catalogue's reading of f. 93r (Kalning, Miller, Zimmermann) and Wattenbach's 'Das ist ein abc' for f. 1r l. 1: i, n, e, d, m, c, a, h, s, t (s, t grade C); f. 44v and the glossary's dotted-box variants not assigned

prior.where: Wattenbach 1869 (broke and described the ciphers, facsimiles and plaintexts of ff. 1r, 5v, 6v); Eis 1957/1982; Heidelberg catalogue 2014 (reads f. 93r). DECODE R2876 'Non-decrypted' is stale.

human: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Opus 5 and posed the oldest-cipher candidate list (research/oldest/CANDIDATES.md A4). Images are free (no login). No target-specific intervention recorded in NOTES or git.
